tip: 'a casa' means home or at home, with no article: Vai a casa.
Polite commands to someone you address as Lei use the subjunctive form: si preoccupi, not preoccupati.
Italian 'has' fear rather than 'is' scared: avere paura = to be scared.
For -ere and -ire verbs, the informal tu command is just the present-tense form: Leggi.
A past yes/no question changes only intonation, with no helper like English 'did': Hai incontrato Marco?
divertirsi is reflexive, literally to enjoy oneself: Ti sei divertita? = Did you have fun?
Getting angry is reflexive in Italian: arrabbiarsi. Ti sei arrabbiata? = Did you get angry?
Passing an exam uses superare, not passare: ha superato l'esame.
arrivare forms the past with essere, so the participle agrees: sei arrivato (m), arrivata (f).
Here 'ci' stands in for 'about it': Ci pensi bene = think it over.
A break is something you 'make' in Italian: fare una pausa.
sbagliare means to get something wrong: hai sbagliato numero = you dialed the wrong number.
Use giocare a before games and sports: giocare a carte.
Before lo or la, the pronoun ti becomes te: te l'ha detto = told it to you.
To need is 'to have need of': avere bisogno di aiuto.
Subject pronouns are usually dropped, since mando already means I send; Io here adds emphasis.
guardare already means to look at, so no preposition follows: abbiamo guardato un film.
entrare needs 'in' before a place: sono entrati nel museo (in + il = nel).
Regular -ere verbs form the past participle in -uto: ricevere becomes ricevuto.
lavare washes something; add -si (lavarsi) to wash yourself: abbiamo lavato la macchina.
In the passato prossimo, conoscere means met for the first time: ha conosciuto una ragazza.
In non...ancora (not yet), ancora sits between ho and the participle: non ho ancora finito.
aprire has an irregular past participle: aperto, not 'aprito'.
Regular -ire verbs form the past participle in -ito: dormire becomes dormito.
Use suonare for playing an instrument, while games use giocare: hai suonato la chitarra.
Magari plus the imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish: magari fossi = I wish I were.
Grocery shopping is fare la spesa, singular; fare spese means to go shopping around.
Italian often uses the 24-hour clock: alle tredici = at 1 pm.
A 'se' clause with the imperfect subjunctive pairs with the conditional: se non piovesse, usciremmo.
suo agrees with the thing owned, not the owner, so it means his or her: il suo compleanno.
With body parts, Italian uses a reflexive plus the article, not a possessive: si è tagliata un dito.
Put fa after a time span to mean ago: molti anni fa = many years ago.
buono shortens to buon before a masculine noun: un buon lavoro.
Decisions are 'taken' in Italian: prendere la decisione = to make the decision.
'se fossi in te' means if I were you, literally if I were in your place.
avessi plus a participle is the past-in-past subjunctive: avessi finito = you had finished.
Weather uses fare: faceva freddo = it was cold, literally it made cold.
